extracted_text: Consideration means something which is of some value in the eye of the law, moving from the plaintiff: it may be some benefit to the defendant, or some detriment to the plaintiff; but at all events it must be moving from the plaintiff.
axiom_summary: Motive is not consideration; a peppercorn or nominal rent moving from the promisee (even if trivial in value) supports the bargain, while moral duty or affection does not.
